title: Grateful Dead Live at Family Dog at the Great Highway on 1969-11-02
venue: Family Dog at the Great Highway
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> SEK'D Prodif Plus -> Samplitude v8.01 Professional -> FLAC
source: Disc 1: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat (44.1k) DDisc 2: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat (44.1k) D

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a monster late‑'69 set featuring an epic Dark Star, stellar St. Stephen, The Eleven and Death Don't Have No Mercy.
ai_review.review: The Charlie Miller‑remastered soundboard is frequently described as crystal‑clear, with superb bass definition – arguably the best quality heard from a ’69 show. Musically the concert shines thanks to a soaring 30‑minute Dark Star that weaves through Chicago‑era riffs and Archie Bell references, followed by powerful St. Stephen, a floating The Eleven and an emotional Death Don't Have No Mercy.

ai_rating.rationale: Nearly all reviewers gave 5‑star ratings (average ~4.9) praising both the performance and the sound quality; the consensus is uniformly enthusiastic.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with exceptional bass clarity; no reported drop‑outs or muffling. Reviewers repeatedly call it the best sound quality they've heard from a 1969 show.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Seamless segues through Dark Star → St. Stephen → The Eleven → Death, with multiple jam detours (Chicago “Only the Beginning”, Archie Bell “Tighten Up”) that keep the momentum high.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as delivering one of his most powerful guitar performances; emotional blues solo on Death and vocal charge on St. Stephen are highlighted.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass clarity praised as “the BEST ever BASS clarity”; no specific performance issues noted.
